intent: To illustrate that younger generations are the primary drivers of Black migration to the South, supporting the narrator's explanation about increased educational opportunities for newer generations.

requirements.question: Should the video explicitly identify 18-29 as the largest group and state 24%, or is the tallest mark enough?
Should the full age-group ranking be explicitly conveyed, or is highlighting the top group sufficient?
Should the video compare 18-29 against the two oldest groups combined (24 vs 22), or only show individual bars?

units.claim: The 18-29 age group has the highest value in the chart, at 24%.

basis.note: Table unit is %; this is the maximum value among the five age groups.

accept: The 18-29 age group has the largest value, 24%.
18-29 is the top age bracket at 24%.
The highest value is the 18-29 group at 24%.
units.evidence: The 18-29 mark must be visibly the highest and labeled or annotated with 24%.

units.claim: The full ranking of age groups by value is 18-29 (24%) > 5-17 = 30-44 (17% each) > 60+ (13%) > 45-59 (9%).
accept: Order from highest to lowest: 18-29 (24%), then 5-17 and 30-44 (17% each), then 60+ (13%), then 45-59 (9%).
18-29 leads; 5-17 and 30-44 tie for second; 60+ is fourth; 45-59 is last.
From highest to lowest, the values are 24%, 17%, 17%, 13%, and 9%.
units.evidence: The relative heights of all five age-group marks must match the ranking, or an on-screen ordered list or labels must show it.

units.claim: The 18-29 group alone (24%) is larger than the 45-59 and 60+ groups combined (9% + 13% = 22%).
accept: The 18-29 group alone (24%) is larger than the 45-59 and 60+ groups combined (9% + 13% = 22%).
24% for 18-29 exceeds the combined 22% for the two oldest groups.
The single 18-29 bracket outweighs the 45-59 and 60+ brackets together, 24 vs 22.
45-59 plus 60+ totals 22%, which is less than the 24% for 18-29 alone.
units.evidence: The 18-29 mark must be shown as taller than the 45-59 and 60+ marks combined, or an annotation must state 24 vs 22.

optional_valid: The 18-29 value is about 1.4 times the 17% values for 5-17 and 30-44 (24 / 17 = 1.41).
The 18-29 value is about 1.8 times the 13% for 60+ (24 / 13 = 1.85).
The 18-29 value is about 2.7 times the 9% for 45-59 (24 / 9 = 2.67).
The three age groups under 45 (5-17 + 18-29 + 30-44 = 17 + 24 + 17 = 58) sum to 58, compared with 22 for 45+ (45-59 + 60+ = 9 + 13 = 22).

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded
